title: An inverse-kernel square enforces one noncommutative word edge
statement: The edge form Q_j is exactly <x-Zy,[Z(I-Z)]^-1(x-Zy)> and is at least 4||x-Zy||^2. It vanishes precisely when x=Zy, without assuming the baseline B commutes with D.

costs: matrix inverses; not a physical implementation
contract.obstruction: Avoids an invalid baseline commutation shortcut; extracted identity, not acceptance of the complete compiler.

evidence.quote: Its zero set is exactly the desired edge recurrence
